+// Copyright IBM Corp. 2026

+
+package git
+
+import (
+	"context"
+	"errors"
+	"fmt"
+	"log/slog"
+	"os"
+	"path/filepath"
+	"strings"
+
+	libgit "github.com/hashicorp/vault/tools/pipeline/internal/pkg/git/client"
+	"github.com/hashicorp/vault/tools/pipeline/internal/pkg/golang"
+)
+
+// SyncGoModFromRef syncs the directives of the go.mod at p in ref, a branch or
+// other revision that git can resolve, into the go.mod at p in dir in the
+// working tree, and writes the result there. It doesn't tidy the module.
+//
+// p is the path of the go.mod, which git resolves from the root of the
+// repository, so we only use it to read from ref and from dir if it's
+// relative to the root of the repository. dir is the root of the repository for
+// a path that comes from a go.work, or "." for a path from the user, which is
+// relative to the working directory like the files we read and write.
+//
+// It's best effort in that it returns a result when the sync fails. The result
+// has the error as its Error.
+func SyncGoModFromRef(
+	ctx context.Context,
+	git *libgit.Client,
+	ref, dir, p string,
+	diffOpts *golang.DiffOpts,
+) (*golang.GoModPathSyncResult, error) {
+	object := ref + ":" + p
+	slog.Default().DebugContext(ctx, "reading source go.mod from ref", slog.String("object", object))
+	showRes, err := git.Show(ctx, &libgit.ShowOpts{Object: object})
+	if err != nil {
+		syncRes := &golang.SyncModRes{
+			Path:  p,
+			Error: fmt.Sprintf("git show %s: %v", object, err),
+		}
+		syncRes.Err = errors.New(syncRes.Error)
+
+		return &golang.GoModPathSyncResult{SyncModRes: syncRes}, syncRes.Err
+	}
+	sourceBytes := showRes.Stdout
+
+	destPath := filepath.Join(dir, p)
+	if err := golang.ValidateGoModPath(ctx, dir, p); err != nil {
+		syncRes := &golang.SyncModRes{Path: p, Error: err.Error(), Err: err}
+		return &golang.GoModPathSyncResult{SyncModRes: syncRes}, err
+	}
+	slog.Default().DebugContext(ctx, "reading dest go.mod from working tree", slog.String("path", destPath))
+	destBytes, err := os.ReadFile(destPath)
+	if err != nil {
+		syncRes := &golang.SyncModRes{
+			Path:  p,
+			Error: fmt.Sprintf("reading %s: %v", destPath, err),
+		}
+		syncRes.Err = errors.New(syncRes.Error)
+
+		return &golang.GoModPathSyncResult{SyncModRes: syncRes}, syncRes.Err
+	}
+
+	// B's name is the file the sync writes to, so it has to be the path in dir.
+	syncReq := &golang.SyncModReq{
+		A:        &golang.ModSource{Name: p, Data: sourceBytes},
+		B:        &golang.ModSource{Name: destPath, Data: destBytes},
+		DiffOpts: diffOpts,
+	}
+	syncRes, err := syncReq.Run(ctx)
+
+	// The result takes its path from B's name. We want the path we were given
+	// instead, which is how the results are matched to the modules of a go.work
+	// and shown, and doesn't depend on where dir is.
+	syncRes.Path = p
+
+	return &golang.GoModPathSyncResult{SyncModRes: syncRes}, err
+}
+
+// WorkspaceGoModPathsFromRef returns the go.mod path of every module in the
+// go.work at the root of ref, a branch or other revision that git can resolve,
+// in go.work order. The paths are relative to the root of the repository. It's
+// an error for ref to have no go.work, or a go.work without modules, so that we
+// never fall back to syncing only the root go.mod while looking like a success.
+func WorkspaceGoModPathsFromRef(
+	ctx context.Context,
+	git *libgit.Client,
+	ref string,
+) ([]string, error) {
+	object := ref + ":go.work"
+	slog.Default().DebugContext(ctx, "reading go.work from ref", slog.String("object", object))
+	showRes, err := git.Show(ctx, &libgit.ShowOpts{Object: object})
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, fmt.Errorf(
+			"listing workspace modules: git show %s: %w: %s",
+			object, err, strings.TrimSpace(string(showRes.Stderr)),
+		)
+	}
+
+	paths, err := golang.GoWorkGoModPaths(object, showRes.Stdout)
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, fmt.Errorf("listing workspace modules: %w", err)
+	}
+	if len(paths) == 0 {
+		return nil, fmt.Errorf("listing workspace modules: %s has no modules", object)
+	}
+
+	return paths, nil
+}

+// Copyright IBM Corp. 2026
+// SPDX-License-Identifier: BUSL-1.1
+
+package git
+
+import (
+	"os"
+	"path/filepath"
+	"testing"
+
+	libgit "github.com/hashicorp/vault/tools/pipeline/internal/pkg/git/client"
+	"github.com/hashicorp/vault/tools/pipeline/internal/pkg/golang"
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
+)
+
+// testGitConfig is the git config our test repositories run with. It gives
+// commits an identity, and stops the global and system config of whoever runs
+// the tests, such as commit signing or a hooks directory, from changing what
+// the tests do. It's set with the git client's WithConfig, which has higher
+// precedence than any config file.
+var testGitConfig = map[string]string{
+	"user.name":      "test",
+	"user.email":     "test@example.com",
+	"commit.gpgsign": "false",
+	"core.hooksPath": "/dev/null",
+}
+
+// TestSyncGoModFromRef verifies that we read the source go.mod from the ref and
+// the dest go.mod from the directory we're given, and not from the working
+// directory of the process, which is where git would resolve a path of its own
+// relative to; that the result has the path we were given rather than the path
+// we wrote to, as the path is how a result is matched to a module of a go.work;
+// and that a go.mod that's missing from either side is reported in the result,
+// as well as returned, so that the sync of the other modules can carry on.
+func TestSyncGoModFromRef(t *testing.T) {
+	t.Parallel()
+
+	const (
+		sourceMod = "module example.com/root\n\ngo 1.21\n\nrequire example.com/dep v1.1.0\n"
+		destMod   = "module example.com/root\n\ngo 1.21\n\nrequire example.com/dep v1.0.0\n"
+	)
+
+	for name, test := range map[string]struct {
+		p           string
+		destFile    string // the go.mod in the working tree
+		wantChanges int
+		wantDest    string
+		errHas      string
+	}{
+		"root go.mod": {
+			p:           "go.mod",
+			destFile:    "go.mod",
+			wantChanges: 1,
+			wantDest:    "example.com/dep v1.1.0",
+		},
+		"go.mod of a module in a directory": {
+			p:           "sdk/go.mod",
+			destFile:    "sdk/go.mod",
+			wantChanges: 1,
+			wantDest:    "example.com/dep v1.1.0",
+		},
+		"missing from the ref": {
+			p:        "missing/go.mod",
+			destFile: "go.mod",
+			errHas:   "git show main:missing/go.mod",
+		},
+		"missing from the working tree": {
+			p:        "sdk/go.mod",
+			destFile: "go.mod", // there's no sdk/go.mod on the branch we're on
+			errHas:   "reading",
+		},
+	} {
+		t.Run(name, func(t *testing.T) {
+			t.Parallel()
+
+			dir := t.TempDir()
+			repo := libgit.NewClient(libgit.WithDir(dir), libgit.WithConfig(testGitConfig))
+			write := func(name, content string) {
+				t.Helper()
+
+				require.NoError(t, os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(filepath.Join(dir, name)), 0o755))
+				require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, name), []byte(content), 0o644))
+			}
+
+			// main has the go.mod we sync from, in the root and in sdk. We then
+			// check out a branch that has older requirements, in the root only
+			// unless the test wants an sdk too.
+			gitRes, err := repo.Init(t.Context(), &libgit.InitOpts{Quiet: true, InitialBranch: "main"})
+			require.NoError(t, err, gitRes.String())
+			write("go.mod", sourceMod)
+			write("sdk/go.mod", sourceMod)
+			gitRes, err = repo.Add(t.Context(), &libgit.AddOpts{All: true})
+			require.NoError(t, err, gitRes.String())
+			gitRes, err = repo.Commit(t.Context(), &libgit.CommitOpts{Quiet: true, Message: "main"})
+			require.NoError(t, err, gitRes.String())
+			gitRes, err = repo.Checkout(t.Context(), &libgit.CheckoutOpts{Quiet: true, NewBranch: "dest"})
+			require.NoError(t, err, gitRes.String())
+			write("go.mod", destMod)
+			if test.destFile == "sdk/go.mod" {
+				write("sdk/go.mod", destMod)
+			} else {
+				require.NoError(t, os.RemoveAll(filepath.Join(dir, "sdk")))
+			}
+			gitRes, err = repo.Add(t.Context(), &libgit.AddOpts{All: true})
+			require.NoError(t, err, gitRes.String())
+			gitRes, err = repo.Commit(t.Context(), &libgit.CommitOpts{Quiet: true, Message: "dest"})
+			require.NoError(t, err, gitRes.String())
+
+			res, err := SyncGoModFromRef(
+				t.Context(), repo, "main", dir, test.p, golang.DefaultSyncDiffOpts(),
+			)
+
+			// Whatever the outcome, the result is the module we were given.
+			require.NotNil(t, res)
+			require.Equal(t, test.p, res.Path)
+
+			if test.errHas != "" {
+				require.ErrorContains(t, err, test.errHas)
+				require.Contains(t, res.Error, test.errHas)
+
+				return
+			}
+			require.NoError(t, err)
+			require.Empty(t, res.Error)
+			require.Len(t, res.Changes, test.wantChanges)
+
+			got, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(dir, test.destFile))
+			require.NoError(t, err)
+			require.Contains(t, string(got), test.wantDest)
+			require.NotContains(t, string(got), "example.com/dep v1.0.0")
+		})
+	}
+}
+
+// TestWorkspaceGoModPathsFromRef verifies that the modules to sync come from
+// the go.work committed at the root of the given ref, in go.work order, and
+// not from the branch that's checked out or the working tree. Falling back to
+// the root go.mod when go.work can't be read would leave every other module
+// unsynced while looking like a success, so a missing, empty, or malformed
+// go.work is an error.
+func TestWorkspaceGoModPathsFromRef(t *testing.T) {
+	t.Parallel()
+
+	for name, test := range map[string]struct {
+		goWork string // the go.work committed on the main branch, if any
+		want   []string
+		errHas string
+	}{
+		"modules in go.work order": {
+			goWork: "go 1.21\n\nuse (\n\t.\n\t./sdk\n\t./api/auth/approle\n)\n",
+			want:   []string{"go.mod", "sdk/go.mod", "api/auth/approle/go.mod"},
+		},
+		"missing go.work": {
+			errHas: "git show main:go.work",
+		},
+		"go.work without modules": {
+			goWork: "go 1.21\n",
+			errHas: "has no modules",
+		},
+		"go.work using a directory outside the repository": {
+			goWork: "go 1.21\n\nuse ../other\n",
+			errHas: "not inside",
+		},
+	} {
+		t.Run(name, func(t *testing.T) {
+			t.Parallel()
+
+			dir := t.TempDir()
+			repo := libgit.NewClient(libgit.WithDir(dir), libgit.WithConfig(testGitConfig))
+
+			// Commit the go.work to main, then check out a branch with a
+			// different go.work and an uncommitted change to it. Neither may
+			// affect what we read from main.
+			gitRes, err := repo.Init(t.Context(), &libgit.InitOpts{Quiet: true, InitialBranch: "main"})
+			require.NoError(t, err, gitRes.String())
+			require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "README"), []byte("fixture\n"), 0o644))
+			if test.goWork != "" {
+				require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "go.work"), []byte(test.goWork), 0o644))
+			}

+// RunGoModDownloadAll executes `go mod download all` in the workspace described
+// by goWork. In workspace mode the go command records the checksums that no
+// module's go.sum holds in go.work.sum, so this brings go.work.sum up to date
+// after the workspace modules' requirements change.
+//
+// We set GOWORK to goWork explicitly, so the go command uses that workspace
+// even when the caller's environment sets GOWORK=off. As with RunGoModTidy, the
+// caller is responsible for GOPRIVATE / GONOSUMDB / GOFLAGS; they're passed
+// through unchanged.
+func RunGoModDownloadAll(ctx context.Context, goWork string) error {
+	if goWork == "" {
+		return errors.New("go.work path is required")
+	}
+
+	goWork, err := filepath.Abs(goWork)
+	if err != nil {
+		return fmt.Errorf("resolving go.work path: %w", err)
+	}
+
+	slog.Default().DebugContext(ctx, "running go mod download all",
+		slog.String("go_work", goWork),
+	)
+	res, err := runGo(ctx, filepath.Dir(goWork), []string{"GOWORK=" + goWork}, "mod", "download", "all")
+	if err != nil {
+		slog.Default().ErrorContext(ctx, "go mod download all failed",
+			slog.String("go_work", goWork),
+			slog.String("output", string(res.Stderr)),
+		)
+
+		// runGo's error names the command and directory but not why it failed.
+		return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s", err, strings.TrimSpace(string(res.Stderr)))
+	}
+
+	return nil
+}
+
+// RunGoModDownload executes `go mod download` for the module at path, with
+// GOWORK=off so the module is resolved from its own go.mod and go.sum rather
+// than the workspace's. The go command records the checksums of every module in
+// the module's build list in its go.sum, including the go.mod checksums of
+// versions a workspace sync raised the requirements to. As with RunGoModTidy,
+// the caller is responsible for GOPRIVATE / GONOSUMDB / GOFLAGS; they're passed
+// through unchanged.
+func RunGoModDownload(ctx context.Context, path string) error {
+	if path == "" {
+		return errors.New("go.mod path is required")
+	}
+
+	dir := filepath.Dir(path)
+	slog.Default().DebugContext(ctx, "running go mod download", slog.String("dir", dir))
+	res, err := runGo(ctx, dir, nil, "mod", "download")
+	if err != nil {
+		slog.Default().ErrorContext(ctx, "go mod download failed",
+			slog.String("dir", dir),
+			slog.String("output", string(res.Stderr)),
+		)
+
+		// runGo's error names the command and directory but not why it failed.
+		return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s", err, strings.TrimSpace(string(res.Stderr)))
+	}
+
+	return nil

+// GoWorkSumSyncResult is the result of bringing the workspace in line with the
+// synced modules with `go work sync` and `go mod download`, which record the
+// checksums the workspace needs in go.work.sum.
+type GoWorkSumSyncResult struct {
+	// Updated is true when go.work.sum changed.
+	Updated bool `json:"updated"`
+	// Error is why the workspace couldn't be synced, including which go command
+	// failed.
+	Error string `json:"error,omitempty"`
+}
+
+// Status describes the result of syncing the workspace in one word.
+func (r *GoWorkSumSyncResult) Status() string {
+	switch {
+	case r.Error != "":
+		return "failed"
+	case r.Updated:
+		return "updated"
+	default:
+		return "unchanged"
+	}
+}
+
+// WorkspaceGoModPaths returns the go.mod path of every module in the go.work in
+// dir, in go.work order, relative to dir. A dir without a go.work has no
+// workspace modules, which returns nil.
+func WorkspaceGoModPaths(dir string) ([]string, error) {
+	goWork := filepath.Join(dir, "go.work")
+	data, err := os.ReadFile(goWork)
+	if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
+		return nil, nil
+	}
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, fmt.Errorf("reading %s: %w", goWork, err)
+	}
+
+	paths, err := GoWorkGoModPaths(goWork, data)
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, fmt.Errorf("listing workspace modules: %w", err)
+	}
+
+	return paths, nil
+}
+
+// SyncWorkspace brings the workspace in dir, the root of the repository, in
+// line with the modules we synced and tidied, in the same way the user would
+// after changing requirements by hand:
+//
+//  1. go work sync raises each module's requirements to the versions the
+//     workspace selects, so that building a module on its own with GOWORK=off
+//     doesn't select lower versions than the workspace does.
+//  2. go mod download all records the checksums that no module's go.sum holds in
+//     go.work.sum.
+//  3. go mod download in each of modules, with GOWORK=off, records the checksums
+//     of the versions step 1 raised the requirements to in that module's go.sum.
+//
+// modules are go.mod paths relative to dir. It returns the files to stage,
+// as paths that start with dir, that aren't a module's go.mod or go.sum:
+// go.work.sum when it changed. A directory without a go.work has nothing to
+// sync, which returns a nil result.
+func SyncWorkspace(ctx context.Context, dir string, modules []string) (*GoWorkSumSyncResult, []string, error) {
+	goWork := filepath.Join(dir, "go.work")
+
+	_, err := os.Stat(goWork)
+	if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
+		slog.Default().DebugContext(ctx, "skipping workspace sync, no go.work found", slog.String("dir", dir))
+		return nil, nil, nil
+	}
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("checking for %s: %w", goWork, err)
+	}
+
+	// A missing go.work.sum is fine; go creates it when it has something to
+	// record.
+	goWorkSum := goWork + ".sum"
+	before, err := os.ReadFile(goWorkSum)
+	if err != nil && !errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
+		return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("reading go.work.sum: %w", err)
+	}
+
+	res := &GoWorkSumSyncResult{}
+	fail := func(err error) (*GoWorkSumSyncResult, []string, error) {
+		res.Error = err.Error()
+		return res, nil, fmt.Errorf("syncing the workspace: %w", err)
+	}
+
+	err = RunGoWorkSync(ctx, goWork)
+	if err != nil {
+		return fail(err)
+	}
+
+	err = RunGoModDownloadAll(ctx, goWork)
+	if err != nil {
+		return fail(err)
+	}
+
+	var downloadErrs []error
+	for _, m := range modules {
+		err = RunGoModDownload(ctx, filepath.Join(dir, m))
+		if err != nil {
+			downloadErrs = append(downloadErrs, err)
+		}
+	}
+	if len(downloadErrs) > 0 {
+		return fail(errors.Join(downloadErrs...))
+	}
+
+	after, err := os.ReadFile(goWorkSum)
+	if err != nil && !errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
+		return res, nil, fmt.Errorf("reading go.work.sum: %w", err)
+	}
+
+	if bytes.Equal(before, after) {
+		slog.Default().DebugContext(ctx, "go.work.sum is up to date")
+		return res, nil, nil
+	}
+
+	res.Updated = true
+
+	return res, []string{goWorkSum}, nil
+}

+// RunGoWorkSync executes `go work sync` in the workspace described by goWork.
+// It raises the requirements in each workspace module's go.mod to the versions
+// the workspace build list selects, so that a module that's built on its own
+// with GOWORK=off doesn't select lower versions than the workspace does.
+//
+// We set GOWORK to goWork explicitly, so the go command uses that workspace
+// even when the caller's environment sets GOWORK=off. As with RunGoModTidy, the
+// caller is responsible for GOPRIVATE / GONOSUMDB / GOFLAGS; they're passed
+// through unchanged.
+func RunGoWorkSync(ctx context.Context, goWork string) error {
+	if goWork == "" {
+		return errors.New("go.work path is required")
+	}
+
+	goWork, err := filepath.Abs(goWork)
+	if err != nil {
+		return fmt.Errorf("resolving go.work path: %w", err)
+	}
+
+	slog.Default().DebugContext(ctx, "running go work sync", slog.String("go_work", goWork))
+	res, err := runGo(ctx, filepath.Dir(goWork), []string{"GOWORK=" + goWork}, "work", "sync")
+	if err != nil {
+		slog.Default().ErrorContext(ctx, "go work sync failed",
+			slog.String("go_work", goWork),
+			slog.String("output", string(res.Stderr)),
+		)
+
+		// runGo's error names the command and directory but not why it failed.
+		return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s", err, strings.TrimSpace(string(res.Stderr)))
+	}
+
+	return nil
